question.text: Backwardation in commodity futures typically occurs due to:

answer.text: Seasonality factors causing current spot supplies to be scarce relative to expected future supply
High interest rates making financing expensive

explanation.text: The Logic: Backwardation arises due to seasonality — during sowing season, spot supplies are scarce (high spot price), while harvesting is expected to increase supply later (lower expected price), so futures trade below spot. The Trap: High interest rates would increase cost of carry and support contango, not backwardation. Speculation and government price controls are not identified by the source as the cause of backwardation. Note: Backwardation in agricultural commodity derivatives is closely tied to the harvest cycle described in the workbook's seasonality discussion.
